settings.unlock.warning.body: Your PIN is kept on this computer, encrypted, so it works after a restart and without a network. It is weaker than your master password: it has far fewer combinations. Anyone who gets a copy of your browser profile (a stolen laptop without disk encryption, malware, a backup or a synced profile folder) can try PINs on their own computer – the five-attempt limit does not apply there. Choose a long PIN, ideally with letters, and use a PIN only on a computer you fully trust that has an encrypted disk. A device that has been revoked can still be opened with its PIN for up to 7 days while it stays offline. A PIN you remove may remain in your browser profile's files on disk. Turn on “Require master password after browser restart” to keep the PIN in memory only.
settings.unlock.warning.title: Read this before you set a PIN
